questions.question_text: Which Azure App Service plan type is best suited for a new web app that requires a pay-as-you-go pricing model and can scale to zero instances?
questions.explanation: The Consumption plan (F1) charges per vCPU-second and instance hour and automatically scales to zero when idle, as described in the Azure documentation (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/app-service/overview-hosting-plan).

questions.question_text: You need to configure autoscale for an App Service plan so that the number of instances increases when CPU usage exceeds 70% and decreases when it drops below 30%. Which setting should you adjust?

options.label: A
options.text: Set the scale rule metric to CPU percentage with thresholds 70% (scale out) and 30% (scale in)

options.label: B
options.text: Set the scale rule metric to HTTP queue length with thresholds 1000 (scale out) and 500 (scale in)

options.label: C
options.text: Set the scale rule metric to memory consumption with thresholds 80% (scale out) and 20% (scale in)

options.label: D
options.text: Set the scale rule metric to request count with thresholds 5000 (scale out) and 2500 (scale in)

questions.explanation: Autoscale rules can be defined using CPU percentage as the metric, with defined thresholds for scaling out and in, according to the Azure documentation (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/app-service/manage-scale).

questions.question_text: Which Azure CLI command creates a .NET 6 web app named 'myapp' in the resource group 'rg1'?
questions.explanation: The command az webapp create with the DOTNET|6.0 runtime creates a .NET 6 web app, as detailed in the Azure CLI reference (https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/webapp/create).

questions.question_text: To bind a custom TLS certificate to a custom domain of an App Service, what is the required first step?

options.label: A
options.text: Upload the certificate to the App Service and then bind it to the domain

options.label: B
options.text: Purchase a certificate from Azure Front Door and associate it with the domain

options.label: C
options.text: Enable HTTPS only in the app settings and the certificate will be applied automatically

options.label: D
options.text: Create a new App Service plan with TLS enabled

questions.explanation: You must first upload the certificate to the App Service, then bind it to the custom domain, as explained in the TLS configuration guide (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/app-service/configure-ssl-certificate).

questions.question_text: You have an existing custom domain 'app.example.com' that you want to map to an App Service named 'mywebapp'. Which DNS record type should you configure?
questions.explanation: A CNAME record that points to the <appname>.azurewebsites.net hostname is the standard way to map a custom domain to an App Service, per the DNS configuration documentation (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/app-service/configure-custom-dns).

questions.question_text: Which setting enables daily backup of an App Service to an Azure Storage account?

options.label: C
options.text: Enable Snapshot in the App Service plan

questions.explanation: The Backup feature in the App Service settings allows you to schedule daily backups to a storage account, as described in the backup documentation (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/app-service/manage-backups).

questions.question_text: To restrict outbound traffic from an App Service to a specific virtual network, which feature should you enable?
questions.explanation: VNet Integration allows an App Service to connect to a virtual network and restrict outbound traffic, as outlined in the networking documentation (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/app-service/web-sites-configure-vnet-integration).

questions.question_text: You need to test a new version of your web app while keeping the production site live. What is the recommended approach?

options.label: A
options.text: Create a staging slot and perform a swap after validation

options.label: B
options.text: Deploy the new version to a separate App Service plan

options.label: C
options.text: Use deployment slots only for backup purposes

options.label: D
options.text: Use the 'Preview' feature to test changes

questions.explanation: Creating a staging slot provides an isolated environment for testing, and a swap can be performed once validation is complete, per the deployment slots documentation (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/app-service/deploy-staging-slots).

questions.question_text: For a web app that experiences moderate traffic and requires SSL support, which App Service plan tier is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: The Standard (S1) tier offers sufficient resources for moderate traffic and includes SSL support, as detailed in the pricing guide (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/app-service/overview-hosting-plan).

questions.question_text: When configuring autoscale based on CPU utilization, which metric should you select?
questions.explanation: CPU Percentage is the metric used for scaling based on processor utilization, as explained in the autoscale documentation (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/app-service/manage-scale).
